Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the chase. The umpires are out in the middle and the West Indies team follows them led by Rovman Powell. Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Mendis will open for Sri Lanka. The first over of the chase will be bowled by Fabian Allen for West Indies.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Considering the nature of the pitch, 162 is a challenging target. The outcome of the match hinges now on Sri Lanka's batting response. If their top order can establish a solid foundation and counter the West Indies bowling attack effectively, they stand a good chance of successfully chasing down the score. The West Indies bowlers, on the other hand, will look for quick wickets and put the Lankans under pressure. So, which side will win the series? We shall find out soon. Chase coming up shortly...

On the bowling front, Sri Lanka initially made inroads into the West Indies batting lineup but were unable to break the pivotal partnership between Powell and Motie in a timely manner. Star bowlers Wanindu Hasaranga and Maheesh Theekshana both claimed two wickets apiece, yet their efforts fell short of stifling the West Indies' recovery.

So, the West Indies have posted a score of 162 runs on the board! After a tumultuous start, the West Indies found themselves in a precarious position at 62 for 5 in the 12th over. However, a crucial partnership between Rovman Powell and Gudakesh Motie provided much-needed stability. This duo stitched together a rapid 54 runs off just 26 balls, allowing the West Indies to regain their footing. After Motie was dismissed, Powell continued to anchor the innings, finishing with a commendable score of 37 runs, propelling the West Indies to a competitive total of 162 runs.
A yorker, on leg, Alzarri Joseph digs it through mid-wicket for a brace. West Indies end their innings at 162/8.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the game to begin! The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Brandon King and Evin Lewis walk in with their blades for the West Indies. Maheesh Theekshana has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

Charith Asalanka, the Sri Lanka skipper says that they would have batted first as well but nothing much changes in the quota of 20 overs. Informs they are unchanged for this game and Pathum Nissanka is fine. Mentions that the side is high on confidence and they just want to continue from where they left.

Rovman Powell, the skipper of West Indies says they will be batting first and mentions that this looks a dry wicket and they'll be looking to put runs on board and defend this. Informs that Shai Hope and Fabian Allen comes in for Andre Fletcher and Shamar Springer. Mentions that this is a pitch where both teams will be looking to play good cricket and 140-150 will be a good total.

West Indies (Playing XI) - Brandon King, Evin Lewis, Shai Hope (WK), Roston Chase, Sherfane Rutherford, Gudakesh Motie, Rovman Powell (C), Romario Shepherd, Fabian Allen, Alzarri Joseph, Shamar Joseph.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Mendis (WK), Kusal Perera, Kamindu Mendis, Charith Asalanka (C), Bhanuka Rajapaksa, Wanindu Hasaranga, Dunith Wellalage, Maheesh Theekshana, Matheesha Pathirana, Nuwan Thushara.
TOSS - The coin lands in favor of West Indies and their skipper Rovman Powell has decided to BAT first.

Home advantage and familiarity with the conditions may tip the scales in Sri Lanka's favor, but the unpredictability and firepower of West Indies make them a formidable opponent. With key player battles and tactical intrigue adding to the excitement, this series finale promises to be an unmissable, high-stakes encounter. It's anyone's game! Sri Lanka and West Indies have the firepower to swing the contest in either side's favor in any situation. Who will emerge victorious? We shall find out soon. Stay tuned for toss and team updates in a bit.

That impressive chase in the first match by West Indies was countered by Sri Lanka's resilient defense in the second, leaving everything to play for in the finale. The Caribbean side's explosive batting will look to replicate their successful pursuit from the opener, while Sri Lanka's revamped bowling attack seeks to repeat their defensive heroics. West Indies will be eager to welcome back Shai Hope, who missed the previous game due to a sore neck, strengthening their batting lineup. Meanwhile, Sri Lanka will rely on the spin wizardry of Wanindu Hasaranga, Maheesh Theekshana and Dunith Wellalage who impressed in the second T20I, to weave their magic once again and outsmart the Caribbean batters

The stage is set for a thrilling finale as Sri Lanka and West Indies clash in the series-deciding 3rd T20I. The two teams are locked at 1-1, ensuring a captivating conclusion to the three-match series.
... MATCHDAY ...

The stage is set for a thrilling finale in the T20I series between Sri Lanka and West Indies at the Rangiri Dambulla International Stadium. After the tourists struck first in the series, the hosts retaliated with a win of their own, leaving fans eager to see who will land the decisive blow in this series decider. West Indies' vulnerabilities against spin were starkly highlighted during their chase of 163 in the previous match, where they crumbled to just 89 runs, with nine out of ten wickets falling to spin. If a similar pitch is prepared for this crucial encounter, the Windies' batters will face a formidable challenge. It’s crucial for the opening pair, Brandon King and Evin Lewis, along with Roston Chase, Sherfane Rutherford, and captain Rovman Powell, to step up. They are also monitoring Shai Hope’s availability after he missed the last game due to a sore neck. On the bowling front, Romario Shepherd excelled in the pace department, while Gudakesh Motie and Roston Chase contributed effectively in the spin department. The two Josephs, Alzarri and Shamar, will need to tighten their game if the tourists hope to pose a serious threat to the Sri Lankan batting unit. On the other hand, Sri Lanka showcased a strong bowling performance but will look to refine their batting approach. Pathum Nissanka stood tall in the previous match, but a collective effort from Kusal Mendis, Kusal Perera, Kamindu Mendis, and skipper Charith Asalanka will be crucial for their chances in this decider. Dunith Wellalage, the debutant, was the standout performer with the ball, supported well by Maheesh Theekshana and Matheesha Pathirana. They will be looking to replicate their impressive performances, if not improve upon them, to secure victory in this final clash. Who do you think will emerge victorious in the decider?
